newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up on spec, local shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up on spec, local shortcovering.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended higher on Wednesday, bolstered by speculative and local shortcovering on the heels of Tuesday's slide to more than three-month lows, dealers said.

Benchmark September contracts rose 3.65 cents a lb on the day, to 161.50 cents, after ranging between 164.25 and 156.00 cents. Spot July, which expires on Monday, ended 2.75 cents higher, at 187.25 cents, while the outer months closed up 0.20 to 2.40 cents.
The July/September switch narrowed to 25.75 cents compared with 26.65 cents at the close on Tuesday, while the September/December switch widened to 13.00 cents from 11.95 cents.
New York coffee prices headed lower at the opening bell, on news of a build-up in U.S. consumer coffee stocks during June.
The Green Coffee Association of New York report after Tuesday's close that supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose in June by 139,000 60-kg bags, to 2,116,000 bags.

Although the increase was mostly in line with expectations, some traders said any build in stocks would set a negative tone. Other traders suspected the increase in inventories was largely priced in the market after Tuesday's sell-off.

Traders said, however, today's activity was mostly technically driven, with light roaster buying toward the lows preventing a test of key chart support at 155.00 cents in the September contract and prompting a spate of speculative and local short-covering.
Upward momentum accelerated after buy-stops were triggered near 157.00-158.00 cents, they said.
"The specs went into the market and decided to explore the downside," said one trader. "This morning roasters came in on this move and forced specs to cover."
The upswing filled a chart gap on the upside formed on Tuesday between 159.50 and 161.00 cents basis September.
Some traders said today's action improved the technical outlook. They pegged September near-term resistance at 165.00 cents. On the downside, the 155.00 level was still seen as strong support.

Other traders said the market's fundamental picture -- including the recent build in exchange-certified coffee stocks and continued mild weather in top-producer Brazil -- was likely to dampen buyers' spirits.
CSCE reported after Wednesday's close that certified coffee inventories rose by 3,269 60-kg bags as of July 15, to 75,414 bags. An additional 39,229 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume was moderate, at an estimated 8,268 lots, traders said.
